items.stem: Describe three human activities that have caused land degradation in India.
items.answer: (1) Mining that leaves deep scars and overburden, as in Jharkhand and Odisha. (2) Overgrazing in Gujarat, Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh. (3) Over-irrigation causing waterlogging and salinity in Punjab and Haryana. (4) Mineral processing such as grinding limestone, whose dust settles on land.

(2) It supports sugarcane, paddy, wheat and other crops, so these areas are densely populated.

items.stem: Describe the three steps involved in resource planning in India.
items.answer: (1) Identification and inventory of resources by surveying, mapping and estimating them. (2) Evolving a planning structure with technology, skill and institutions for implementing plans. (3) Matching resource development plans with overall national development plans.

items.stem:
(a) "The availability of resources is a necessary but not a sufficient condition for development." Examine with examples. (3 marks)
(b) Why is resource planning essential in India? (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) (1) Resources need technology and institutions to be used. (2) Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh are rich in minerals but have remained backward. (3) Arunachal Pradesh has abundant water but lacks infrastructure. (4) Regions with good institutions and technology, like Punjab, have developed. (b) (1) India has enormous diversity in the availability of resources. (2) Some regions are rich in some resources but poor in others, so balanced development needs planning.

items.stem:
(a) Explain three problems caused by the indiscriminate use of resources. (3 marks)
(b) Why is resource planning essential in India? (2 marks)

(2) Some regions are rich in some resources but poor in others, so balanced development needs planning.
